claims: Left-click selects a specialist on the status bar or field and issues movement; right-click deselects. Control+left-click-drag groups specialists; Alt+left-click-drag selects only creatures when mixed with specialists.

Contextual action prompts initiate creature tasks. Engineer builds by selecting a building option; Control+left-click invokes its destroy command. Botanist uses Control+left-click to cut plants. Ranger Control+left-click kills enemy creatures or culls owned creatures.
Geneticist researches unknown creatures, heals injured lifeforms, and stuns researched creatures. Ranger can feed, boost fighting, enable mating in season, and stun.
Network chat uses F1-F4 for opponents and Return to send; manual describes IPX networking.

The screen includes base-power display, GOOP storage, score-o-rama, Bad-o-meter, five specialist monitors, action screen, help toggle, overview map, and field of play. Strength, health and creature genetic evolution are shown; Botanist monitor uses that bar for seed count.
Monitor click selects and right-click zooms; red static indicates a specialist taking damage. Score-o-rama tracks mission completion and can show opposing teams after a Tech Facility is built.

Five specialist roles are described: Engineer (build/repair/upgrade), Geneticist (research/heal/stun), Botanist (plant/harvest seeds/cut plants), Ranger (creature behavior/population), and pilot (interplanetary travel). Initial crew is selected by Ethereals; later missions allow team choice and expertise is displayed by cursor hover.
The Landing Pad supports crew transfers from orbit and later crew selection.

Extractor mines minerals into GOOP and is required before other buildings. First Stage Power Distributor channels power to nearby structures and can run itself plus one Extractor; Photon Processor converts stellar energy to electrical power and requires a Distributor.

Gene Pod breeds basic drones from GOOP. The manual lists cost, strength, defense, speed and awareness attributes; it says to build a Gene Pod before the buildings listed after it. Recycling Plant converts dead flora/fauna to GOOP; GOOP Vat stores surplus and requires a Recycling Plant.

Landing Pad moves crew between orbit and planet. Pulper makes upgrade mouldings from wood and requires Crabs to upgrade buildings. Other building types are revealed after early missions; Gene Machine/Gene Lab are named for advanced hybrid research.

GOOP is the currency/material for buildings and creatures. Plants and dead biomass feed GOOP production through creature labor and Recycling Plant; plant wood can supply a Pulper for upgrade mouldings.

Building upgrades require an Engineer, powered Pulper, at least one Mule and one Crab. Mule carries harvested plant material to Pulper; Crab carries mouldings to Engineer and assists construction. Higher Engineer skill shortens upgrade time.

Natural creature families named are Mule, Crab, Frog, Bird, and Dino. The Gene Pod supports basic drones; research above the 50% Gene Pod ceiling needs Gene Machine or Gene Lab. The manual says a 50% research reading is enough to build, and extra research affects size, strength, stamina, and intelligence.

Different creatures may mate to produce hybrids; a Mule and Crab can produce Crabomule. Hybrids combine parent abilities, count as their own species, and do not inherit species special powers automatically. The manual calls for a Monolith interaction to grant a hybrid power.
A Monolith can raise specialist abilities and grant a species special power. Listed powers: Mule kick, Crab armor, Frog damaging spit, Bird dive attack, Dino fire breath.

The four playable races are Earthlings, Saurians, Bohemians and Schnozzoids; Ethereals are non-playable observers. Race descriptions give qualitative ability, strength, speed, research, creature-attention, healing, and cloaking traits. Monolith-upgraded specialist ability/strength maxima are race-specific.
Creature descriptions characterize Mule as labor/biomass transport, Crab as builder and land/water-capable, Frog as scout, Bird as flying scout, and Dino as powerful but temperamental.

Plants have climatic/terrain preferences and vary in GOOP, food, wood and defensive value. Botanist harvest reveals a species icon and surface preference; symbol sizes indicate food and wood value and a dot indicates seed cost.

Early examples include Terrinium Bulb (grass), Phylax Root (grass, fast-growing and nutritious), and Waxx Leaf (grass, reproduces quickly). Manual hints mention later plant types but do not provide a complete species catalog.

Single-player campaign is described as 24 planets/missions to repopulate. The first five hint levels are Exceland, Krell, Madami, Roach and Brown. Goals and available systems differ by mission; Ethereals give orders and the player is judged on them.
Some missions use Ethereal Zones and competing colonization teams; the manual says computer players may compete. Zone mission hints describe moving creatures to marked Zones and depleting them.

Bad-o-meter reflects Ethereal approval. Good actions may lead to rewards such as Monolith; bad behavior may be punished, including Adami Process. The manual uses qualitative terms and provides no numeric thresholds or event formula.

Network winner depends on level: score most in Ethereal Zones where present, or defeat opponents on levels without Zones. Single-player mission end conditions are not specified as a complete formal rule set.

Options screen diagram labels music toggle and level, sound-effects toggle and level, save new file by typing a name and pressing Return, load saved game, finish game and return to the main screen, exit to system, and exit screen.
Pilot handles travel between planets after a left-click. Landing Pad supports specialist crew transfer.

Network option appears when suitable IPX network is detected. Manual describes creating/joining sessions, host-selected level, eight levels, opponent chat using F1-F4, and creature advantage. The manual does not establish a player cap.
Creature advantage picks one pure breed from Dino, Crab, Frog, Bird at 50% research with its special ability active.

The manual mentions computer colonization players and creatures following instincts when deactivated from player control; it does not define opponent strategy, pathfinding, threat evaluation, orders, or autonomous behavior rules.
The UI labels save-new-file and load-saved-game actions, but the manual does not specify file format, serialized state, checkpoints, campaign selection semantics, or save timing.

Numeric costs, production rates, resource capacities, power radii, plant growth rates, creature stat formulas, breeding probability/timing, genetics inheritance calculations, damage, tick timing, map dimensions, mission scripts, AI rules, and save schema are not specified by this manual.

No contradictions were identified within the summarized manual sections. Product notice states the product may change without notice, so manual claims need comparison with a hash-identified executable build.

binary_execution_verification.note: This manual lane performed no game-binary execution or binary analysis. All rule claims are manual-documented only.

prioritized_questions_for_sol: Map the manual command affordances to actual executable command identifiers, mouse/key event state, targeting modes and group-selection rules; in particular resolve Engineer selection/upgrading ambiguity and context-action prompts.

Recover mission objective predicates, Ethereal arrival/timer logic, Bad-o-meter updates/rewards/punishments, and campaign transition order; check whether the first five hint names and 24-planet count match the CD candidate build.
Determine the actual economy and power model: Extractor inputs/output, GOOP/storage capacities, resource transactions, power range/consumption, Photon Processor generation and upgrade effects.
Determine creature creation/research stat formulas, Gene Pod cap and Gene Machine/Lab unlocks; identify breeding compatibility, mating season, offspring inheritance and hybrid species registration.
Identify plant growth/harvest/replant, terrain suitability, food/wood values, biomass collection and recycling behavior; test whether Bad-o-meter rewards sustainable farming as described.
Trace specialist and creature autonomy, Ranger task areas, combat/damage/stun behavior, pathfinding and computer opponent decision logic.
Find save/load routines and file schemas, plus campaign state persistence; distinguish save UI claims from the actual implementation.
After matching executable hashes/layouts, cross-check manual-only findings against each relevant build and report variant-specific differences.
